## The three findings

| # | ID | Charge | Sev / Conf | agent_risk | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `crime_00007` | Route Metadata Drift — `/settings/billing` | medium / 0.65 | 0.38 | **Warn** (block if the PR touches this route or either nav file) |
| 2 | `crime_00006` | Duplicated Navigation Source — `/settings/billing` | medium / 0.70 | 0.38 | **Warn — same defect as #1, one fix** |
| 3 | `crime_00033` | Docs-Code Drift — `docs/teams.md:5 → ./setup.md` | low / 0.90 | 0.24 | **Block if the diff broke it**, otherwise warn |

---

### 1. `route_metadata_drift` — `src/routes/settings/billing.tsx` → **warn**

One destination carries four competing names:

- path `/settings/billing` · file `billing.tsx`
- component `PricingPage`
- `metadata.title: Plans` · `<title>: Subscription`
- nav labels: `Plans` (registry) / `Billing` (sidebar)

This is the highest-value of the three for agent risk: an agent told to "rename the Plans page" has four plausible targets and no way to tell which is canonical, so it renames one and leaves three stale — exactly the state the repo is already in.

Not a block on its own, though. Confidence is 0.65 (the detector can't know whether `<title>: Subscription` is deliberate user-facing copy vs. drift), churn is 0, and it's pre-existing. Blocking a merge on a naming inconsistency the PR didn't introduce is how teams learn to bypass the gate. **Block only when the diff touches `src/routes/settings/billing.tsx`, `src/nav/registry.ts`, or `src/nav/sidebar.ts`** — if you're in there anyway, converge the names before adding a fifth.

### 2. `duplicated_navigation_source` → **warn, and fix it as part of #1**

Same destination, same two files, same label conflict — `crime_00007`'s evidence already contains `crime_00006` in full. These are one defect seen through two detectors, not two items for the backlog. Filing them separately gets you two half-fixes.

The ordering matters: fix #2 first (collapse `registry.ts` + `sidebar.ts` into one nav source, or mark one canonical in a comment), and #1 shrinks to "align component name and the two titles." Fixing #1 first leaves the duplicate source in place, so the labels can diverge again on the next edit.

Same gating rule: warn by default, block if the PR edits either nav file.

### 3. `docs_code_drift` — `docs/teams.md:5 → ./setup.md` → **conditional block**

Lowest severity, but the only one that's objectively, deterministically wrong: the file either exists or it doesn't. Confidence 0.90, effort quick, zero judgement required — which makes it the one finding here that's actually good CI-gate material.

Split by provenance:

- **The PR deleted/renamed `setup.md`, or added the link → block.** A dangling link introduced by the diff is a regression with a one-line fix, and it's precisely the failure mode that misroutes an agent reading the docs for setup instructions.
- **Pre-existing → warn.** Fix it in the same pass, but don't gate an unrelated merge on it.

Nothing here justifies **ignore**. The closest candidate is `<title>: Subscription` inside #1, if that turns out to be intentional copy — suppress that single evidence line, not the finding.

---

### Context worth carrying into the fix

These three aren't isolated. The scan also has three `orphaned_destination` findings (`/account/subscription`, `/team`, `/workspace/members` — `crime_00029`–`31`) and `concept_alias_drift` on the tenant group (`crime_00019`: account / organisation / team / workspace across five files). Same root cause: **no single source of truth for destinations or for the vocabulary naming them.** The `/settings/billing` fix is the cheap, well-evidenced entry point; if you land the consolidated nav source, the orphan checks become meaningful instead of noise.
